title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Commemorative Coin Act
official_summary:
FIFA World Cup 2026 Commemorative Coin Act

This act directs the Department of the Treasury to mint coins in commemoration of the FIFA World Cup 2026 to be held in the United States, Mexico, and Canada.

All surcharges received by Treasury from the sale of the coins shall be promptly paid by Treasury to FWC2026 US, Inc. (the U.S.-incorporated FIFA subsidiary operating the FIFA Men's World Cup 2026) for the purpose of aiding soccer programs and activities in the United States.

summary.headline: A federal law directs the Treasury to mint commemorative coins for the 2026 FIFA World Cup and send the coin surcharges to a U.S. FIFA subsidiary for soccer programs.
summary.what_it_does: The law requires the Department of the Treasury to mint coins honoring the FIFA World Cup 2026, which will be held in the United States, Mexico, and Canada. Treasury must promptly pay all surcharges collected from coin sales to FWC2026 US, Inc., the U.S. subsidiary of FIFA that runs the men's tournament. The money is to be used for soccer programs and activities in the United States. The summary does not list coin designs, mintage numbers, or surcharge amounts.

who_it_affects.group: People who buy the commemorative coins
who_it_affects.how: Buyers would pay the coin surcharges, which go to FWC2026 US, Inc. for U.S. soccer programs.
The company receives the coin surcharge proceeds from the Treasury for soccer programs and activities in the United States.
Programs and activities in the United States may receive funding from the coin surcharge proceeds.
Treasury must mint the coins and transfer the surcharge money promptly to the designated company.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 11, 2024. The official summary does not give a specific date for coin release or surcharge payments.
